name: reject-alg-substituted-hs256
description: An unlock request an issuer must refuse whole: the same signed resource behind a header that says HS256, MAC'd with the publisher's public key. THE ATTACK. The payload segment is the publisher's again, and the header names {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT","kid":...} under the publisher's own kid. The third segment is HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 bytes of "<header>.<payload>", keyed by substitution.macKey - the public key that kid names, taken as the uncompressed P-256 point. Those bytes are published: they are in this file, and an issuer holds them because holding them is how it verifies anything at all. WHY THE SECOND ARM. An implementation can refuse "none" as a special case, since it reads like an obvious hole, and go on dispatching on the header for everything else. This token names an algorithm such an implementation can genuinely run, over a key it genuinely holds, and it verifies - HMAC does not care that its secret was published, only that both sides used the same bytes. The MAC is real; the algorithm is the lie. What the ES256 arm of reject-forged-resourcejwt is to a damaged signature, this is to a token that merely carries none. WHICH BYTES, and it matters to a replay: an implementation confusing the two key types MACs with whatever serialization of the public key it has in hand - the point, a PEM, the JWK as text. This vector uses the point and records exactly those bytes, so an implementation that keeps its key that way is caught here, and one that keeps it another way is caught by the header check that should have run before any of this. The rule covers every serialization: the algorithm comes from the issuer, never from the token. A CONFORMANT ISSUER answers 400 with bad_alg, on the header, before a key is consulted - the same refusal its sibling gets, at the same cost of nothing. expected.privateKeyReached is false. NOT CONFORMANT: verifying this MAC and reading the payload, however carefully the payload is treated afterwards. NOTHING IN THIS rawBody MOVES BETWEEN RUNS: a MAC over stable bytes is stable, so this file, like its sibling, has no segment that changes when the vectors are regenerated. REPLAY. Post `rawBody` VERBATIM - the string as it sits in this file, never a re-serialization of it - to the unlock endpoint, with `issuer` as the key material the issuer holds for its own name and keyId, and `publisher.signingKeys` as the public verification halves, read straight from this file rather than resolved by a deployment lookup. A pass is: expected.code where there is one; key material back for exactly the coordinates in expected.keys and no others; and an error back for exactly the coordinates in expected.errors, under the codes recorded there. No publisher private key is in this file, on purpose: an issuer never holds one, so everything a reject vector asks for is checkable with what a real issuer has. HOW FAR THE REFUSAL REACHES IS PART OF WHAT IS PINNED, and expected.privateKeyReached says which side of the line this body lands on. A request that fails integrity - a signature that does not verify, a signed resource with no renderId to bind to - has asked nothing that could be answered, so it is refused whole and before the key store is consulted at all. A blob presented at a coordinate it was not sealed at is one bad blob in an ordinary request: the only way to find out is to try it, so the key store is reached, the blob comes back as an error, and everything else the request carried is answered beside it. The untouched coordinates were never the attack, and a page has to keep working around one bad blob, so they are answered. Everything in the body but the attack is the render this vector was cut from - the envelope, the periodKeys section and the untouched blobs are what the publisher emitted. An unchanged regeneration retains the valid resourceJWT signature segment inside rawBody, so the body is byte-stable with seal-ecdh.json. A fresh seal still draws a new k, which is why a replayer verifies the segment rather than comparing it. The token is the one in the base vector from the same run, byte for byte, except in reject-no-renderid, reject-renderid-noncanonical and reject-renderid-wrong-width, whose envelopes are second tokens signed over resources with the renderId removed, given a noncanonical spelling, or resized, which is each vector's whole subject; in reject-forged-resourcejwt, whose signature segment was drawn by a key the publisher does not hold; in reject-tampered-resourcejwt, which carries the seal-ecdh token's own signature segment under a payload edited after signing; and in the two reject-alg-substituted arms, which carry that token's payload segment under a header rewritten to name another algorithm, with a third segment that is empty or a MAC - neither of which moves between runs.

substitution.macKeyIs: publisher.signingKeys[0].publicKeyJwk as the uncompressed P-256 point, 0x04 || x || y, 65 bytes
